description: We are students at Folsom Lake College interested in everything programming.
summary: We aimed to create a Google Maps style navigator for the Martian terrain, specifically around the landing site of the Curiosity rover. In order to ensure safe traversal to the locations of key findings from Curiosity's journey (or any location in the surrounding area), our program displays the optimal path for astronauts to get to a selected location from wherever they currently are. It accounts for elevation, wind stress, slope inclination, distance, and shade data to produce routes that avoids as many hazards as possible.
details: As of submission, our project is only a barebones demo of the full program we envisioned. It simply renders a png image based on hard-coded parameters for the person's location/rotation, where they want to go, and what type of underlying map they want displayed (mosaic, topographic, slope inclination, or wind stress). The result is a clear route for the astronaut to follow to get to wherever they need to go, along the safest path for them to take. Our path finding algorithm and some data collection/extraction is written in C++, while our renderer and most data collection/extraction is written in Python.
